items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: My daddy's name is John Handy Sr.

ctx.x: Were your family musical? Everybody. What about your father, mother and your grandfather now?

Well, I don't know my grandfather. He died before I was big enough to know him. But my daddy played violin. My mother was a pianist. My sister's a pianist. My brother's a guitarist. And I got one player's bass. The one player's guitarist named Julius Handy. My sister's named Mary Louise Handy. My mother's name is Elizabeth Handy. My daddy's name is John Handy Sr.
What did you say your daddy played? Violin.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: And then later I started playing drums with him. I played drums with him for about three years.

ctx.x: 19. 19-under. Did your family play actually? Everybody in my family play or something.
Yeah, I mean before you? Yeah. Did daddy play? Yeah, my daddy was in the fall once. What was his name? John Handy. John Handy. That was all of his name? He didn't have a middle name?

That's all your name, huh? No, my name is John Guy Handy, but I don't use the Guy Handy. John Handy. Somebody slipped cap in there, I mean. Yeah. Where did you get that cap? A.J. Minor. Uh-huh. How did that come about, I mean? Oh, this rehearsal was the only Pelican and I heard some bad notes and I stopped the band.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-15
items.q: I don't know how long my dad had had that record. I used to hear him play it a lot. He used to play it a lot on Sundays when his band used to come down at a rehearsal.

ctx.x: And your father had had the record for a number of years.

I'll tell you the truth. I don't know how long my dad had had that record. I used to hear him play it a lot. He used to play it a lot on Sundays when his band used to come down at a rehearsal. Mm-hmm. And they played that record a lot to learn it. And they learned to play it pretty good too. Yeah, that particular record they learned it pretty good.
But when you say that record was hot music, jazz music, just like they played here in 1920s? Was it on that style? No, no, no, no.
